- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underreact to true price spikes — correct by adding 1–2% to forecast for early spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 30d mean), model often overcorrects downward — cap forecast decline at 1–2% below peak to avoid overshoot.
- If official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates downside risk — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward lower range.
- When sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.50) and supply net is negative, model tends to overestimate recovery — reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3% per day to reflect lagged sentiment impact.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model often fails to capture early bearish momentum — adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% for first 5–7 days if sentiment is bearish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish/bearish alternation, model overfits to recent trend — apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast to avoid false momentum capture.
